issues.description: Entire compiled script transmitted in every compile response inflates payload regardless of download intent.
issues.detail: script_content is always read and returned even when the user never clicks download. For large pipelines this bloats every RPC response and Jupyter front-end state. Consider a separate on-demand RPC endpoint (e.g., get_compiled_script(path)) that streams the file only when requested.

issues.description: File read uses default encoding and no error handling, can fail on non-ASCII locales.
issues.detail: open(script_path) without encoding='utf-8' relies on the system default (e.g., ASCII on some servers), which can raise UnicodeDecodeError for pipelines containing non-ASCII identifiers or comments. Also no try/except: a read failure now breaks the entire compile RPC, regressing the prior success path.

issues.description: Download button rendered even when compiledContent is undefined, producing a silent no-op.
issues.detail: The GetAppIcon is unconditionally rendered in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick guards on props.compiledContent and silently returns if absent. If backend or older sessions omit script_content, the user sees a download icon that does nothing. Either gate rendering on compiledContent or surface an error.

issues.description: Download icon lacks keyboard accessibility and button semantics.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon is rendered as an SVG with onClick but no role=button, tabIndex, or onKeyDown handler. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot trigger the download. Wrap it in a <button> or IconButton with aria-label to match the adjacent anchor's accessibility.

issues.description: Fallback filename 'pipeline.kale.py' is unreachable and misleading.
issues.detail: split('/').pop() on a non-empty string only returns falsy for a trailing slash, which compiledPath won't have. The || fallback is dead code; if defensive, prefer deriving from pipeline_name. Minor, but worth simplifying for clarity.

issues.description: Compiled script content lingers in React state and memory after download.
issues.detail: compiledContent is stored on DeployProgressState alongside compiledPath and persists for the session. For large notebooks compiled repeatedly this accumulates memory. Consider clearing it after successful download or fetching lazily on click.

review.summary: The feature works for the happy path but ships the entire compiled script in every compile RPC response, even when the user never downloads. The backend read is also encoding-unsafe and lacks error handling, which can regress the existing compile flow. On the frontend, the download icon is always rendered but silently no-ops when content is missing, and it lacks keyboard/ARIA semantics expected of an interactive control. An on-demand fetch endpoint would address the bandwidth, memory, and robustness concerns at once.
